In February 2021 a car-sized rover was lowered on cables into Jezero Crater. Its job: read the rocks of an ancient lake, look for signs of past life, and seal the most promising samples in tubes that a future mission could bring home.

In July 2024 Perseverance found a rock nicknamed "Cheyava Falls" with "leopard spots". In September 2025 NASA described its sample, "Sapphire Canyon", as containing a potential biosignature — not proof of life.

In July 2024 Perseverance found an arrowhead-shaped rock in an ancient river valley. It was covered in pale spots with dark rims. The core sample taken from it was named "Sapphire Canyon". In September 2025 NASA announced that the minerals in those spots — linked to vivianite and greigite — are a potential biosignature.
